from.place: Proof paragraph 2, the finite-coefficient mapping-complex adjunction before R lim: the enriched tensor cocontinuity foundation in the inherited ancestry, specifically the space-colimit base-change input to the labelled spine/prism horn calculus; Kerodon 05V5 uses slice cartesian closure via 05UY.

title: Cartesian closure of coherent slices of spaces
statement:
Use spaces, coherent functors, mapping spaces and homotopy pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and let $\mathcal S$ be the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces, formed in a containing universe. For a $\mathcal U$-small space $B$, let $\mathcal S_{/B}$ be the coherent slice: its objects are arrows to $B$, and its transformations include the homotopies commuting with these arrows and all higher compatibilities. For objects $X\to B$ and $Y\to B$ there is an object $[X,Y]_B\to B$ with $\mathcal U$-small total space and an evaluation map $[X,Y]_B\times_B X\to Y$ over $B$ such that evaluation and composition induce equivalences of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{/B}}(T,[X,Y]_B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{/B}}(T\times_B X,Y)$$
for every $T\to B$. These equivalences are coherent and natural in $T$, $X$ and $Y$; equivalently, $-\times_B X$ has a coherent right adjoint $[X,-]_B$. Products here are homotopy pullbacks of spaces. Empty spaces and empty fibers are allowed.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 7.7.3.17 (Tag 05UY), with the definition of cartesian closedness in Subsection 7.7.3. The proof constructs the small relative simplicial exponential of Kan fibrations over B, proves it fibrant by right properness, and passes to the coherent slice. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Kerodon tags are not Stacks tags; no Stacks tag states coherent cartesian closure of space slices.

proof.text: Fix a $\mathcal U$-small Kan model of $B$. Let $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ be the simplicial category of small Kan complexes, enriched by $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(Z,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Z\times\Delta^n,Y)$. For a Kan fibration $g:Y\to B$ and any small simplicial set $Z$, the map $\operatorname{Fun}(Z,Y)\to\operatorname{Fun}(Z,B)$ is a Kan fibration: transposing a horn-lifting problem gives a lifting problem for $g$ against $Z\times\Lambda_i^n\to Z\times\Delta^n$. The latter is anodyne by the cited pushout-product theorem, applied to $\varnothing\to Z$ and the horn inclusion; the Kan model structure makes each horn inclusion a trivial cofibration. Taking $Y\to\Delta^0$ shows that the mapping complexes of $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ are Kan. Define $\mathcal K_B$ to be its full strict enriched slice on the Kan fibrations to $B$. If $g:Y\to B$ is such an object, $Y$ is Kan, since horn lifting first in $B$ and then along $g$ fills every horn in $Y$. Thus these really are objects of the enriched slice, including $\varnothing\to B$. The strict slice mapping complexes are Kan as well: a horn in the fiber of $g\circ-$ over a vertex $f$ is a horn upstairs over the constant simplex $f$, so the lifting property from this step fills it in that fiber. Thus $\mathcal K_B$ is locally Kan.

source.place: Example 5.5.1.23, mapping-fibration hypothesis, expanded by pushout-product horn lifting.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-fibration-slice-nerve-equivalence] to the chosen $\mathcal U$-small Kan model $B$. Its $\mathcal K_B$ is exactly the enriched category of step 1: the objects are small Kan fibrations to $B$ and the morphism complexes are the same strict fibers of postcomposition. It supplies a fully faithful and essentially surjective coherent comparison $J:N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal K_B\to\mathcal S_{/B}$, together with its source compatibility. In particular the strict mapping fibers compute the coherent mapping spaces, and every arrow to $B$ is equivalent over $B$ to a small Kan-fibration representative. The comparison includes the commuting triangles and their higher compatibilities, so source projections are retained. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to this fully faithful $J$; its essential image is the whole slice by the cited essential surjectivity. We therefore obtain a coherent quasi-inverse with coherent unit and counit. It suffices to construct evaluation and the mapping equivalences in $\mathcal K_B$ and carry them through $J$.

source.place: Example 5.5.1.23, now cited as a separate Kan-fibration/coherent-slice comparison theorem; the original comparison and inverse-over-base arguments are preserved as the new node obligation.

proof.text:
Represent the two objects by Kan fibrations $f:X\to B$ and $g:Y\to B$. Construct a simplicial set $M$ over $B$ as follows: an $n$-simplex is a pair $(\sigma,\rho)$ consisting of $\sigma:\Delta^n\to B$ and a simplicial map $\rho:\Delta^n\times_B X\to Y$ whose composite with $g$ is $\sigma\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^n}$. A simplicial operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ sends this pair to $(\sigma\alpha,\rho\circ(\alpha\times_B1_X))$. Associativity of precomposition proves the simplicial identities. Projection sends $(\sigma,\rho)$ to $\sigma$. Define evaluation $M\times_B X\to Y$ in degree $n$ by $((\sigma,\rho),x)\mapsto\rho_n(1_{[n]},x)$. It is simplicial by the same restriction formula. For every simplicial set $K\to B$, a map $h:K\to M$ gives a map $K\times_B X\to Y$ by this evaluation. Conversely a map $v:K\times_B X\to Y$ over $B$ assigns to each simplex $k:\Delta^n\to K$ the pair $(\sigma_k,v\circ(k\times_B1_X))$. These assignments commute with restriction and are inverse, simplex by simplex. Consequently
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{/B}(K,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{/B}(K\times_B X,Y),$$
with the bijection induced by actual evaluation. This is an explicit construction, not a choice from a mere existence claim. Each set $M_n$ is $\mathcal U$-small: it is a small union, indexed by $B_n$, of subsets of sets of simplicial maps between $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets. The countable collection of degrees remains in $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Proposition 7.7.3.17, displayed construction of the relative simplicial exponential; degreewise currying and universe check written out.

proof.text: The projection $M\to B$ is a Kan fibration. Given a horn inclusion $i:A=\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow D=\Delta^n$ and a square from $i$ to this projection, transpose by step 3. The desired lift becomes a lift from $i_X:A\times_B X\to D\times_B X$ against $g:Y\to B$. The projection $D\times_B X\to D$ is a Kan fibration, by pulling back horn lifts for $f$. The map $i_X$ is its pullback of the weak homotopy equivalence $i$. Right properness in the cited Kan model theorem makes $i_X$ a weak homotopy equivalence. It is also degreewise injective, so is a trivial cofibration, and the model lifting axiom gives the required lift against $g$. Transposing it back solves the original horn problem. Since $B$ is Kan, $M$ is Kan by lifting first in $B$ and then in $M$. Thus the small $M\to B$ is an object of $\mathcal K_B$. No fibers have been assumed inhabited.

source.place: Proposition 7.7.3.17, final horn/anodyne lifting argument using Proposition 3.4.0.2 (0109); right properness is the existing Kan-model node.

proof.text:
The enriched category $\mathcal K_B$ has terminal object $1_B:B\to B$ and products given by strict pullbacks. A product $T\times_B X\to B$ is again a Kan fibration, by pullback and successive horn lifting. For any $V\to B$ the defining strict mapping complexes satisfy
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{/B}(V,T\times_B X)=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{/B}(V,T)\times\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{/B}(V,X),\qquad \underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{/B}(V,1_B)=\Delta^0,$$
since a map into the pullback is exactly its two projections over $B$, in every simplicial degree. The coherent-nerve mapping comparisons and the mapping-space limit criterion therefore exhibit these actual projection cones as products and the indicated object as terminal in $N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal K_B$. These products have the required meaning on total spaces: for fibrations to the Kan base, the strict pullback computes the homotopy pullback by the Kan model theorem. The functor $J$ constructed in step 2 preserves their source projections, so $J$ carries them to the specified products in $\mathcal S_{/B}$.

source.place: Remark 7.7.3.9, finite enriched products, specialized to Kan fibrations; strict versus homotopy pullback checked explicitly.

proof.text:
Apply the bijection of step 3 to $K=T\times\Delta^n$, with structure map through $T\to B$. The identity $(T\times\Delta^n)\times_B X=(T\times_B X)\times\Delta^n$ gives
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{/B}(T,M(X,Y))\cong\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{/B}(T\times_B X,Y).$$
Restriction of a simplex on either side is precomposition by $1_T\times\alpha$, so these degreewise inverse currying assignments form an isomorphism of simplicial sets, induced by the actual evaluation of step 3. Apply [lem-coef-enriched-exponential-nerve-criterion] to $\mathcal A=\mathcal K_B$ and $E(X,Y)=M(X,Y)$. Step 1 gives its locally Kan hypothesis; step 5 gives the enriched terminal and product isomorphisms; steps 3-4 ensure the chosen exponential objects lie in $\mathcal K_B$; and the displayed isomorphism verifies its evaluation hypothesis. The criterion supplies the enriched bifunctor on these very objects, its natural evaluation, and the coherent right adjoint to product with $X$ on the nerve. Its mapping equivalences are induced by this evaluation and composition and are coherently natural in $T,X,Y$, including arbitrary simplex parameters. Thus this uses the explicit small construction, not an unspecified bijection on components.

source.place: Remark 7.7.3.9, conditions (1)-(3); the enriched bifunctor and coherent-nerve adjunction are extracted as a general statement-only criterion.

proof.text: Use the coherent quasi-inverse of $J$ from step 2 to choose representatives for arbitrary $T,X,Y$ in the coherent slice, and apply $J$ to $M$, its evaluation, and the mapping equivalences of step 6. The unit and counit equivalences of this quasi-inverse identify their inputs with the original objects; step 5 identifies the product appearing in evaluation with $T\times_BX$. Composition of these coherent equivalences yields the claimed coherent mapping equivalences, naturally in $T,X,Y$. Its representing object has $\mathcal U$-small total space by steps 3-4 and the source compatibility of $J$. If $B=\varnothing$, all objects and this exponential are empty and the slice is terminal. If $X=\varnothing$, the construction has exactly one $\rho$ over each $\sigma$, so $M=B$; if $Y=\varnothing$, a simplex occurs precisely when its pullback of $X$ is empty. Thus the construction and argument include empty spaces and empty fibers without adding a hypothesis.

source.place: Proposition 7.7.3.17, passage from the enriched Kan-fibration model to the coherent slice; empty cases and small total space made explicit.
